units.caption: Supplementary Fig. 3 | Duration and environmental differences among near-peak representations. a,b, Empirical cumulative distributions of cyclone-level covered durations over valid 6-h intervals in 2,340 main-sample histories (a), including the 123 recurrent cyclones shown separately in b. R is the continuous episode containing the first LMI; Longest is the longest episode in the anchored domain; U is the union of qualifying episodes from that onset; F encloses U. Later occupancy  and weakening bridges  satisfy . c, Paired whole-window environmental contrasts,  and , in recurrent cyclones (factor-specific n = 120–123). Only the averaging windows change; each cyclone's environmental record is fixed. These are differences between window means, distinct from means of isolated later-occupancy or bridge components. Factors and native units are SST (°C), 200–850-hPa shear (m s⁻¹), mid-level RH (percentage points), 200-hPa divergence (10⁻⁵ s⁻¹), ascent (; Pa s⁻¹) and hemisphere-signed 850-hPa vorticity (10⁻⁵ s⁻¹), sampled at 200–800 km. Contrasts are divided by fixed lifecycle reference SDs. Duration curves use cyclone-level observations; means and their marginal intervals are reported in Table S1a. In c, columns show paired means and whiskers show marginal 95% percentile intervals from 2,000 paired SID resamples. Supplementary Fig. 33 gives whole-cohort and component-mean comparisons; Table S1b and figure sources provide native estimates, intervals, counts and reference parameters. Table S1a also reports means and intervals for the longest episode, later occupancy and bridges.
